extracted.intended_audience: IP applicants, patent/trademark/design attorneys, and IP office practitioners (domestic and foreign) interested in Indonesian IP procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Country fact sheet from DGIP/WIPO describing legal requirements, registrability standards, procedural timelines and remedies for patents, utility models, industrial designs, trademarks and copyright in Indonesia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive requirements for patentability include novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability; adequate disclosure is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent term: 20 years (10 years for utility models). Utility models: protect inventions which are new and industrially applicable; they do not need an inventive step. (Law No.13/2016; table: Novelty, Industrial applicability, Inventive step, Disclosure). Responsible authority: DGIP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-patentable subject matter (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories of subject-matter excluded from patent protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes discoveries; discovery of scientific rules and theories; mathematics; business plans, regulations or methods; mental treatments or gambles; human and animal treatment; microorganisms and components of natural microorganisms; extracts from animals or plants; inventions/devices contrary to state peace and social order, health, environment, rules and laws, and national good traditional cultures (Art.9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of local agent and language for patent filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applicants must file through a local agent; filings must be in Indonesian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application filed by an inventor or applicant who does not reside or have domicile in Indonesia must be filed through a local agent (art.28). Indonesian language required (art.24). If claims and description are in English they must be submitted with Indonesian translation no later than 30 days from filing date (art.34).

rubrics_metrics.name: Grace period rules for patent novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Limited pre-filing disclosures that do not defeat novelty under specified conditions and time windows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 6 months before filing: disclosures from exhibitions (international or officially recognized national exhibitions) or exploitation in Indonesia in context of experimentation/R&D. 12 months before filing: disclosures due to breach of an obligation to preserve confidentiality (Art.6).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent publication and opposition window
rubrics_metrics.description: When patent applications are published and third-party opportunity to submit comments/objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DGIP publishes patent application 18 months after filing date or priority date (art.46-48). Third parties may file comments and/or objections to the patent application within 6 months from publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination request deadline (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Time limit for requesting substantive examination in order to avoid deemed withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must request substantive examination within 30 months from the filing date for national filings; for PCT national phase the deadline is 31 months. Otherwise, the application is deemed withdrawn. DGIP then conducts substantive examination and may invite amendments if non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision notification and post-decision remedies (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing for DGIP decision after examination and available remedies following grant or refusal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DGIP notifies applicant of decision to grant or refuse within 36 months from the request for examination. In case of refusal the applicant may file an appeal petition to the Patent Appeal Commission. In case of grant third parties may file a lawsuit for revocation to the Commercial Court.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT national phase requirements and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules for entering national phase from an international (PCT) application designating Indonesia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT international applications designating Indonesia should be translated into Indonesian and enter the national phase within 31 months from the priority date. Filing fees must be paid at national phase. Applicants should request substantive examination within 31 months from international filing date; the rest of procedure aligns with national applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formality examination and correction periods (patents)
rubrics_metrics.description: DGIP formality check and time allowed to cure formal deficiencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DGIP carries out a formality examination; if application does not comply, DGIP invites the applicant to amend the application within 3 months. If corrections are not made, application remains non-compliant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design filing content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: What must be included in an industrial design application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must include drawings, photographs or other adequate graphic representations of the design, a description of the design for which protection is sought, and an indication of the kinds of products for which the industrial design will be used (Law No.31/2000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design registrability exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Designs that cannot be registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designs contrary to prevailing laws and regulations, public order, religion or morality are non-registrable (art.4). Indonesia is not a party to the Hague Agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial design examination, publication and objection procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Process and timelines for design publication, objections and substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DGIP carries out formality examination and invites amendments within 3 months if needed. DGIP publishes the design application within 3 months from filing date. Third parties may file objections during 3 months from publication date. DGIP carries out substantive examination when it receives objections and issues a decision whether to approve or refuse the objection. Where there is no objection DGIP shall grant a Certificate of Industrial Design. If refused, applicant may file a lawsuit with the Commercial Court within 3 months from notification of refusal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of local representative for industrial designs
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign applicants must use a registered local consultant for design filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant who resides outside Indonesia must file an application through a consultant on intellectual property rights who is registered at DGIP (art.1). Language: Indonesian Bahasa (art.11(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark subject-matter and types
rubrics_metrics.description: Kinds of signs and protected subject-matter under Indonesian trademark law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protected subject-matter includes Trademarks, Service Marks, Collective Marks, Geographical Indications, Sources of Origin (Law No.20/2016).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registrability and absolute grounds for refusal
rubrics_metrics.description: Absolute and relative grounds that prevent trademark registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-registrable: application by an applicant in bad faith; marks contrary to prevailing rules/regulation, morality, religion or public order; marks not having distinctive character (generic or descriptive); marks that have become public property; marks constituting information related to the goods/services; marks similar in essential parts or entirety with an earlier registered mark for same/similar goods/services; marks similar to known geographical indications (Art.20-21). Additionally marks must be capable of being represented graphically (art.5 and 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark formality, publication and opposition timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Key procedural timelines for trademark applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DGIP carries out formality examination and may invite amendment within 2 months. DGIP publishes applications in the Mark Gazette not later than 15 days from filing; publication lasts 2 months. Any party may file an opposition within the 2-month publication period. DGIP commences substantive examination if there is no opposition not later than 30 days from expiration of publication. DGIP notifies the applicant of decision to grant or refuse within 150 days after commencement of substantive examination (Art.14–23).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark post-decision remedies and cancellation period
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals and actions available following grant or refusal of a trademark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of refusal, applicant may file an appeal with the Trademark Appeal Commission. In case of a decision to grant, third parties may file a lawsuit for cancellation to the Commercial Court within 5 years from the date of registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Madrid System (international trademark) handling by DGIP
rubrics_metrics.description: How international (Madrid) applications are handled and timeline for provisional refusals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For international applications where DGIP is the office of origin or a designated office, DGIP carries out substantive examination within specified timelines. For international extension requests DGIP carries out substantive examination within 18 months from receiving the request for extension of protection from WIPO; Registrar may issue a provisional refusal and invites the applicant to respond within 30 days. Rest of procedure aligns with national filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright subject-matter and originality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Definition of a 'work' and who is an 'author' for copyright protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Work' protected is result of works of an author which shows originality in the field of science, arts and literature (art.1 and 2). Author: person(s) who individually or jointly produce works that are unique and personal (art.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright exclusive rights and moral rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights granted to authors under Indonesian copyright law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes right to be named as author; right to oppose changes to a work; rights to demonstrate works in public; publicize works; reproduce or adapt works; disseminate original works or copies to the public (Art.5 and following).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations and exceptions to copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Permitted uses that do not constitute infringement subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted when sources are fully cited and do not prejudice normal interest of the author: use for education, thesis, research, scientific reporting, criticism/review; excerpts for advocacy in or out of court; reproduction for the blind (Braille) unless commercial; limited reproduction by public libraries, educational or scientific institutions and documentation centers of non-commercial nature solely for conducting their activities (Art.43–49).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Terms of protection for various categories of copyrighted works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copyright valid for life of author plus 70 years (art.58). Copyright on computer programs, cinematographic works, photographic works, databases and works from adaptations is valid for 50 years from first publication (art.59). Copyright owned by a legal entity is valid for 50 years from first publication (art.58).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement of local representative for trademarks (foreign applicants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign trademark applicants must use a local consultant registered with DGIP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant who resides outside the country must file an application through a consultant of intellectual property rights registered at DGIP and the mark must be capable of being represented graphically (art.5 and 7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals and judicial remedies across IP types
rubrics_metrics.description: Forums and remedies available after administrative decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patents: appeal to Patent Appeal Commission; post-grant revocation to Commercial Court. Trademarks: appeal to Trademark Appeal Commission; cancellation action in Commercial Court within 5 years from registration. Industrial designs: applicant may file lawsuit with Commercial Court within 3 months from notification of refusal. General: DGIP issues invitations to correct; repeated non-compliance results in refusal/withdrawal.
